1	"""wiring_check.py — OWNER BASELINE GATE: assert every routed cell's EXECUTED
2	path is the L3-TC persistent megakernel (bf16 wgmma engine), fail LOUD otherwise.
3	
4	Mandated by the locked baseline directive: "build a wiring_check.py: route every
5	cell, assert executed path == L3-TC, fail loud — saved to repo, run before every
6	roofline." This is the per-cell pass/fail oracle for the 33 (model × optimizer)
7	cells; the roofline must not be measured until this reports the converted set.
8	
9	WHAT IT DOES (no surrogate, no inference from gate logic — it OBSERVES the real
10	executed engine):
11	  * For each (model, optimizer) cell it runs a few REAL race train steps via the
12	    production train_<opt> function (grokking_race_v2.OPTIMIZER_REGISTRY), with
13	    the SAME dispatch wrapper the roofline uses to capture grokking_race_v2.
14	    LAST_L3_ENGINE — the engine dispatch.cpp ACTUALLY ran ("wgmma" | "scalar" |
15	    None). dispatch.cpp has no silent wgmma->scalar fallback, so a captured
16	    engine=="wgmma" PROVES the bf16 tensor-core L3 megakernel executed.
17	  * A cell PASSES iff every timed step fired engine=="wgmma" (path == L3-TC) AND
18	    the stale-ABI latch never tripped (a TypeError soft-degrade would mean the
19	    extension predates the widened fused_step ABI — rebuild, then re-run).
20	  * A cell is BLOCKED otherwise; the row records the OBSERVED path (eager /
21	    eager+L1-fused-tail / L3-scalar) and a cited reason so the converted/blocked
22	    table is self-documenting.
23	
24	USAGE
25	  python wiring_check.py                       # all 33 cells, table + JSON
26	  python wiring_check.py --models decoder      # subset
27	  python wiring_check.py --opts adamw,lion     # subset
28	  python wiring_check.py --require-all         # exit 1 unless ALL routed cells
29	                                               # are L3-TC (the FULL-baseline gate)
30	Default exit code: 0 if the run completed (the converted/blocked split is the
31	deliverable); --require-all makes a non-fully-converted run fail loud (exit 1),
32	which is the gate the locked directive's end-state wants green.
33	
34	Output JSON: results/h100_grokking_race/wiring_check.json
35	"""
36	from __future__ import annotations
37	
38	import argparse
39	import json
40	import sys
41	import traceback
42	from pathlib import Path
43	
44	ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
45	OUT = ROOT / "results" / "h100_grokking_race"
46	
47	# The 33 cells. Optimizer keys are the RACE registry keys (note: the race uses
48	# "supergrok" for the SuperGrok11 cell; dispatch/codegen use "supergrok11" — the
49	# train fn owns the mapping, so we drive by the race key and let it translate).
50	MODELS = ["decoder", "vit", "mamba"]
51	OPTS = ["adamw", "neuralgrok", "grokadamw", "supergrok", "supergrok15",
52	        "supergrok2", "grokfast", "muon", "lion", "looksam", "prodigy"]
53	
54	# Cited reasons a cell cannot (yet) be L3-TC. Keyed by the OBSERVED engine/path so
55	# the table explains every non-converted cell from the single source of truth
56	# (INTEGRATION-OPTSTAGES.md verdict table + dispatch.cpp _L3_WGMMA_CELLS + the
57	# fused_train_step registries). These are diagnostic annotations, not gates — the
58	# GATE is the observed engine. A blocked cell still fails the --require-all gate.
59	_BLOCK_REASONS = {
60	    # optimizer -> short reason (why its L3-TC tail is not wired on the prod path)
61	    "looksam": ("MODEL-COUPLED: st.sam_dir needs a SAM 2nd backward in the model "
62	                "phase (INTEGRATION-OPTSTAGES §6); model-stage-owned, not wired."),
63	    "supergrok": ("MODEL-COUPLED 2nd-pass (OPTSTAGES §4): SG11's `sharpness` is "
64	                  "(g_sam−g)² from a SAM SECOND backward at perturbed weights — a "
65	                  "FULL second in-kernel model fwd+bwd+dW-assembly (perturb→2nd "
66	                  "backward→restore), the SAME model-stage machinery as looksam, a "
67	                  "DIFFERENT category from the per-element/precompute tails "
68	                  "(prodigy-d, muon-NS) that were in scope. The per-tensor mu/gate "
69	                  "meta-MLP precompute sits ON TOP of that 2nd pass. NOTE: the missing "
70	                  "`sharpness` FusedOptState field is cheap (append-only, as aux_* "
71	                  "proved) but INSUFFICIENT — the second fwd+bwd pipeline is the real "
72	                  "blocker. A host-side 2nd backward feeding st.sharpness would be an "
73	                  "intermediate launch (violates single-persistent-launch). Probed "
74	                  "re-invocable (vittc_forward_tile/vittc_backward_tile are device "
75	                  "fns) but the unit of work is the whole P1+P2 pipeline, twice."),
76	    "supergrok15": ("MODEL-COUPLED 2nd-pass (OPTSTAGES §5): same blocker as SG11 — "
77	                    "SG15's `sharpness` is a SAM SECOND-backward side-channel needing "
78	                    "a FULL second in-kernel model fwd+bwd+dW-assembly. SG15 is "
79	                    "SIMPLER than SG11 in the tail (gate is a host scalar, no cosine "
80	                    "stage) but identical at the blocking layer: the 2nd pass is "
81	                    "model-stage machinery, out of the per-element-tail scope. The "
82	                    "missing `sharpness` field is cheap but insufficient (the 2nd "
83	                    "fwd+bwd is the real cost)."),
84	    "supergrok2": ("MODEL-COUPLED 2nd-pass + SEPARATE-LAUNCH precompute (OPTSTAGES "
85	                   "§7/INTEGRATION-NOTES): the sg2_meta_tail is PARITY-PROVEN as a "
86	                   "STANDALONE kernel (sg2_meta_optimizer_tail, its own <<<>>> "
87	                   "launch), but it CONSUMES pre-computed host inputs it cannot "
88	                   "produce in the single vit launch: (i) `sharpness_packed` — the "
89	                   "SAME SAM 2nd-backward side-channel as SG11/15 (needs a 2nd in-"
90	                   "kernel fwd+bwd), AND (ii) `perm_packed`/`unsort_packed` — a "
91	                   "per-tensor SEGMENTED-SORT permutation (a separate sort stage), "
92	                   "plus the CSA/HCA/PEER/GRU meta-net weight pack. It is NOT a drop-"
93	                   "in P2.x/P3 tail slot like grokadamw/prodigy/muon; wiring it into "
94	                   "the single persistent launch needs the 2nd-pass pipeline AND an "
95	                   "in-kernel segmented sort — model-stage + separate-launch "
96	                   "machinery, both out of scope."),
97	    "prodigy": ("STAGED global-d, CONVERTED for decoder+vit (wave-2): the cross-all-"
98	                "tensors d-reduction is the in-kernel P2.6 phase + the owner-block "
99	                "beta3-EMA/d_coef/persist (OPTSTAGES §2). Only mamba×prodigy is still "
100	                "blocked (no mamba P2.6 wiring) — decoder/vit fire wgmma."),
101	    "muon": ("STAGED grid-cooperative NS, CONVERTED for vit (wave-2): the 11 2D "
102	             "weights' Newton-Schulz orthogonalization is the in-kernel P2.7 phase "
103	             "(grid-barrier-looped, no separate launch); the 1D weights take the P3 "
104	             "AdamW tail with INDEPENDENT aux_lr/aux_betas (the eager non-2D group, "
105	             "carried by the append-only FusedScalars aux_* widening). OPTSTAGES §3. "
106	             "decoder/mamba×muon are still blocked (no P2.7 wiring there) — vit fires "
107	             "wgmma; if vit×muon shows here, the kernel rebuild is stale."),
108	    "neuralgrok": ("KERNEL-READY, RACE-BLOCKED (directive item d): the psi MLP is in "
109	                   "opt_components.cuh (kPsiHidden=16 == race neural_hidden=16, 2-layer), "
110	                   "so a snapshot-plumbed L3 step would PASS the tail gate (m/v parity "
111	                   "validates the psi pack; clip is inert at steps 1&50, max grad-norm "
112	                   "0.72<1.0). BUT train_neuralgrok trains the amplifier BETWEEN steps via "
113	                   "a differentiable Python rebuild that needs the model grads, and the L3 "
114	                   "megakernel returns only the loss — snapshot-plumbing alone yields a "
115	                   "frozen-amplifier (non-faithful) race. The race integration (re-extract "
116	                   "+ keep the amplifier-training half) is deferred; needs owner re-scope."),
117	    # grokadamw (decoder): CONVERTED in this cycle (no longer blocked) — all THREE
118	    # eager mechanisms land in the bf16 TC path: (i) per-tensor layer-wise β1 +
119	    # rebased bc1 in the kernel P3 (t == flat layer index); (ii) GLOBAL grad-norm
120	    # clip via the kernel's P2.5 deterministic global-norm reduction (γ/grad_clip
121	    # thread through FusedScalars); (iii) adaptive-α is a no-op in-context (no
122	    # losses fed to .step()), so the static α is faithful. So decoder×grokadamw
123	    # should be OBSERVED as wgmma; if it ever shows here, the kernel rebuild is
124	    # stale. vit×grokadamw is ALSO CONVERTED now (wave-2 vit lane — the same 3
125	    # mechanisms on the vit TC kernel: P2.5 global-norm clip + P3 per-tensor β1),
126	    # so it too should be OBSERVED as wgmma, not listed here.
127	}
128	# Per-(model) note for any cell that routes to a scalar L3 megakernel rather than
129	# wgmma (mamba's measured carve-out — the path EXISTS but scalar wins on wall).

364	// Per-(device, n) reusable scratch for fused_step. The barrier counters and the
365	// `acts` proxy were previously reallocated (and `acts` memset over the full
366	// param size) on EVERY dispatch; sizes/offsets are constant for a given n.
367	// We persist them keyed by (device_index, n) and only reset the mutable parts
368	// (zero the 3 barrier counters + the acts buffer) per step. Behavior is
369	// identical — same zero-initialized scratch handed to the launcher — but the
370	// allocations/the full-size memset of sizes/offsets happen once per shape.
371	struct FusedScratch {
372	 torch::Tensor g_next;       // int32 [1]
373	 torch::Tensor g_arrived;    // int32 [1] (reinterpreted as unsigned)
374	 torch::Tensor g_generation; // int32 [1] (reinterpreted as unsigned)
375	 torch::Tensor sizes;        // int32 [1] = n  (constant per n)
376	 torch::Tensor offsets;      // int32 [1] = 0  (constant)
377	 torch::Tensor acts;         // float [numel(params)] proxy buffer

380	// Keyed by (device_index, n). n disambiguates differing param shapes on the
381	// same device; acts is sized to params.numel() (== n here, single flat tensor).
382	inline FusedScratch& fused_scratch_for(const torch::Tensor& params, int64_t n) {
383	 static std::unordered_map<long long, FusedScratch> cache;
384	 const long long dev_idx =
385	 params.device().is_cuda() ? static_cast<long long>(params.device().index())
386	 : -1LL;
387	 const long long key = (dev_idx << 40) ^ static_cast<long long>(n);
388	 auto it = cache.find(key);
389	 if (it == cache.end()) {
390	 auto opts_i =
391	 torch::TensorOptions().device(params.device()).dtype(torch::kInt32);
392	 FusedScratch s;
393	 s.g_next = torch::zeros({1}, opts_i);
394	 s.g_arrived = torch::zeros({1}, opts_i);
395	 s.g_generation = torch::zeros({1}, opts_i);
396	 s.sizes = torch::full({1}, n, opts_i); // constant for this n
397	 s.offsets = torch::zeros({1}, opts_i); // constant
398	 s.acts = torch::zeros_like(params);
399	 it = cache.emplace(key, std::move(s)).first;
400	 } else {
401	 // Reset only the mutable scratch; sizes/offsets are invariant for this n.
402	 it->second.g_next.zero_();
403	 it->second.g_arrived.zero_();
404	 it->second.g_generation.zero_();
405	 it->second.acts.zero_();
406	 }
407	 return it->second;
408	}

Now I have a clear picture of the architecture. This is the critical insight: the `wgmma_tail_opt_id` function returns `-1` for supergrok2 (and SG11/15/looksam), which means these optimizers do NOT have a single-launch TC path. The dispatch's `dec_l3_real`/`vit_l3_real` gates require `dec_opt_id >= 0`, so supergrok2 never enters the L3-TC megakernel path through `fused_step`.

The `_BLOCK_REASONS["supergrok2"]` documents exactly why: `sg2_meta_tail` is a STANDALONE kernel that consumes pre-computed host inputs (`sharpness_packed` = SAM 2nd-backward, `perm_packed`/`unsort_packed` = segmented sort) that it cannot produce inside the single persistent launch.

I now have a thorough understanding of the architecture and the fundamental tension. Let me consult the advisor before any substantive work, because there's a critical conflict between my task directive and the documented `_BLOCK_REASONS["supergrok2"]`.

Key facts I've established:
1. `wiring_check.py` reports `path=L3-TC-megakernel(wgmma)` ONLY when `LAST_L3_ENGINE["engine"]=="wgmma"`, set by `_try_fused_train_step` after `fused_train_step` succeeds via dispatch.cpp's wgmma branch.
2. `fused_train_step`/dispatch.cpp's wgmma path runs the model fwd+bwd+optimizer-tail in ONE persistent megakernel. The optimizer tail is `apply_optimizer<Opt>` selected by `opt_id`. `wgmma_tail_opt_id("supergrok2")` returns `-1`.
3. `train_supergrok2` (the production train fn) doesn't even call `_try_fused_train_step` — it's fully eager.
4. The documented blocker: `sg2_meta_tail` is a STANDALONE kernel (its own `<<<>>>` launch) that consumes `sharpness_packed` (SAM 2nd-backward), `perm_packed`/`unsort_packed` (segmented sort) — inputs it can't produce inside the single model fwd+bwd launch.

The conflict: `wiring_check.py` only registers `wgmma` for the SINGLE persistent fwd+bwd+tail megakernel. A standalone `sg2_meta_optimizer_tail` launch (even if composed into `train_supergrok2`) would NOT set `LAST_L3_ENGINE["engine"]=="wgmma"`, so wiring_check would still show eager. Let me verify this understanding by checking how `sg2_meta_optimizer_tail` is exposed and whether `LAST_L3_ENGINE` could be set by it.

"""Standalone A/A/A determinism probe for ANY (model, opt) wgmma cell.

Replicates test_l3tc_tail_gate._one() 3x and reports L/G/P run-to-run equality
SEPARATELY (the advisor's bisection: L-diverge=>forward, G-diverge=>backward,
P-only=>opt tail). Works for cells NOT in _CELLS (drives fused_train_step
directly with gemm_impl="wgmma"). Diagnostic only — not a committed gate.

Usage: python -m tests.hw._aaa_probe <model> <opt> [n_runs]
"""
import sys
import torch
from tests.hw.test_l3tc_tail_gate import _build_cell, _g  # reuse the seeded builder
from grokking_optimizers.dispatch import canonicalize_model, fused_train_step


def _opt_factory(g, model, opt):
    """Build the live race optimizer for (model, opt) with production hyperparams,
    mirroring the per-opt factories in the gate. Generic: pulls OPTIMIZER_CONFIGS."""
    c = dict(g.DEFAULT_CONFIG)
    c.update(g.OPTIMIZER_CONFIGS[opt])
    c.update({"model_type": model, "p": 97})
    return c


def _one(model, opt):
    canon = canonicalize_model(model)
    g, c, m, data, dev = _build_cell(model)
    tx, ty = data[0], data[1]
    # Live optimizer with production hyperparams (the gate's factories do this; we
    # reuse the race's own builder so scalars match the production path exactly).
    fn = g.OPTIMIZER_REGISTRY[opt]
    # We only need the optimizer object; build it the way the gate factories do.
    # The gate uses spec["factory"]; here we construct via the race's train-fn-free
    # path: instantiate the optimizer class the same way train_<opt> would.
    opt_obj = _build_opt_like_race(g, m, opt, c)
    cc = {}
    L, G = fused_train_step(canon, opt, m, opt_obj, tx, ty, state_cache=cc,
                            step=1, return_grad=True, gemm_impl="wgmma")
    total = sum(p.numel() for _, p in m.named_parameters() if p.requires_grad)
    P = torch.empty(total, device=dev)
    o = 0
    for _, p in m.named_parameters():
        if p.requires_grad:
            k = p.numel(); P[o:o + k].copy_(p.data.reshape(-1)); o += k
    return float(L), G.clone(), P


def _build_opt_like_race(g, m, opt, c):
    """Instantiate the optimizer the way the race's train_<opt> does, for the opts
    we probe (grokadamw, neuralgrok, prodigy, muon). Minimal — just enough scalars."""
    import grokking_optimizers as go
    params = m.parameters()
    lr = c["lr"]; b1 = c["beta1"]; b2 = c["beta2"]; wd = c["weight_decay"]
    if opt == "grokadamw":
        from grokking_optimizers.optimizers.grokadamw import GrokAdamW
        return GrokAdamW(params, lr=lr, betas=(b1, b2), weight_decay=wd,
                         grokking_signal_fns=None)
    if opt == "neuralgrok":
        from grokking_optimizers.optimizers.neuralgrok import NeuralGrok
        return NeuralGrok(params, lr=lr, betas=(b1, b2), weight_decay=wd)
    if opt == "prodigy":
        from grokking_optimizers.optimizers.prodigy import Prodigy
        return Prodigy(params, lr=lr, betas=(b1, b2), weight_decay=wd)
    if opt == "muon":
        from grokking_optimizers.optimizers.muon import Muon
        return Muon(params, lr=lr, momentum=c.get("muon_momentum", 0.95),
                    weight_decay=wd)
    if opt == "adamw":
        return torch.optim.AdamW(params, lr=lr, betas=(b1, b2), weight_decay=wd)
    raise SystemExit(f"no probe factory for opt={opt}")


def main():
    model = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "mamba"
    opt = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else "prodigy"
    n = int(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else 3
    runs = [_one(model, opt) for _ in range(n)]
    Ls = [r[0] for r in runs]; Gs = [r[1] for r in runs]; Ps = [r[2] for r in runs]
    L_eq = all(Ls[0] == x for x in Ls)
    G_eq = all(torch.equal(Gs[0], x) for x in Gs)
    P_eq = all(torch.equal(Ps[0], x) for x in Ps)
    # max abs deltas (vs run 0) for the diverging tensors
    g_maxd = max((Gs[0] - x).abs().max().item() for x in Gs[1:]) if n > 1 else 0.0
    p_maxd = max((Ps[0] - x).abs().max().item() for x in Ps[1:]) if n > 1 else 0.0
    print(f"[aaa] {opt}/{model}  n={n}")
    print(f"  loss : {'  '.join(f'{x:.7f}' for x in Ls)}  L_eq={L_eq}")
    print(f"  grad : G_eq={G_eq}  max|dG|={g_maxd:.3e}")
    print(f"  param: P_eq={P_eq}  max|dP|={p_maxd:.3e}")
    verdict = ("FORWARD (L diverges) -> shared model_stage_mamba_tc.cuh -> CITE"
               if not L_eq else
               "BACKWARD/grad (G diverges, L ok) -> shared grad-assembly -> likely CITE"
               if not G_eq else
               "PARAM-only (L,G ok) -> opt tail (fused_mamba_megakernel P2.6/P3) -> FIX"
               if not P_eq else
               "CLEAN A/A/A (all bit-identical)")
    print(f"  => {verdict}")
    sys.exit(0 if (L_eq and G_eq and P_eq) else 2)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
